newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Shell Australia year net income falls.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Shell Australia year net income falls.

text.p: Shell Australia said on Monday its net income for calendar 1996 was A$277 million compared with A$399 million in 1995, but that it expected improved earnings in 1997.
Shell Australia said also it was reviewing its involvement in the oil products refining and marketing operations in Australia because of what it described as unacceptable profitability.
Shell Australia is a unit of Royal Dutch/Shell group.
"A strong operating performance from upstream oil and natural gas provided a reasonable result despite a disappointing return from oil products and a loss for coal," Shell said in a statement.
The company said its capital expenditure rose by A$77 million to A$407 million in calendar 1996, mainly reflecting the development of the the Dartbrook underground coal mine in New South Wales.
Speaking to reporters, Shell Australia Chairman and Chief Executive Roland Williams said he expected the group's overall earnings to improve in 1997.
"Improved performance is expected from all the coal operations, supported in particular by the contributions of the first full year's production from Dartbrook," Williams said.
He said the coal division contributed a loss of A$7 million before financing costs in 1996, mainly due to a A$30 million provision on the closure of the South Bulli coal mine.
Williams said the company expected better earnings from its oil products division which contributed A$97 million before financing costs.

"The profitability of our oil products business, at less than one cent per litre, is totally unacceptable. Our continued involvement in refining and marketing is now the subject of the most fundamental review with capital expenditure for the entire sector severely cut back to a care and maintainance level while we reassess our position," Williams said.
He said Shell Australia was dissatisfied and concerned by the slow speed of deregulation which prevented it competing on an equal basis with independents and impeded necessary restructuring.
"Under the current circumstances, we see the likelihood of refinery closures and associated job losses," he said.
